title: Green peas, fresh, cooked with oil

content.title: About
content.content: Green peas are young pods or seeds of the pea plant (Pisum sativum) harvested fresh and lightly sautéed in vegetable oil. They have a sweet, delicate flavor, a tender yet slightly crisp texture, and a vivid green color.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Peas belong to the legume family and have been cultivated for over 7,000 years.
Fresh peas contain more vitamin C than dried peas.
In Russia and many CIS countries peas are traditionally used in soups, stews, and salads.
Sautéing in oil helps retain most nutrients while adding a richer aroma.
Pea plants fix nitrogen in the soil, improving its fertility.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and enhances iron absorption.

items.title: Source of plant protein
items.content: Peas provide about 5 g of protein per 100 g, making them a good protein source for vegetarians.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and helps maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains folate
items.content: Folate is essential for DNA synthesis and is especially important during pregnancy.

items.title: Contains healthy fats
items.content: The small amount of vegetable oil adds energy and assists absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to peas, ranging from skin rashes to severe symptoms.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Peas contain oxalates, which can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible people.

items.title: Sodium from added salt
items.content: When prepared with salted oil, sodium levels can be high; use minimal salt.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Peas can be enjoyed as a snack, added to salads, soups, stews, pasta dishes, or blended into a puree. Serve with a sprinkle of fresh herbs and a squeeze of lemon juice for brightness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked peas in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3–4 days. For longer storage, freeze portions in sealed bags.
